request.prompt: View 2, the same castle seen from straight above, a top-down plan view with north at the top of the frame, at dusk in rain. The frame is tall. At the bottom centre a small roofless square shrine on green valley ground; a straight road runs north from it to a square stair tower, from which a long narrow stone bridge on piers runs north to a gatehouse at the south edge of a large grey rock crag that fills the upper two thirds of the frame. On the crag: north of the gatehouse a very large open paved courtyard in the centre-right. A thin stone shelf path, clearly visible, leaves the gatehouse's south face just west of the bridge, runs west along the foot of the crag's south cliff to the south-west corner, turns and runs north along the foot of the west cliff, and ends at the west end of a long stable block that sits on the crag's west edge south-west of the courtyard. North of the stables a small scriptorium, then a square cloister with open arcades and a lawn, then a long chapel lying east-west with its rose-window front facing west. North-west corner: a square bell tower. East of the cloister a narrow lane, then the keep: a big great hall directly north of the courtyard, a small antechamber north of it, and a big throne hall north of that. Along the whole north edge a long thin high walk joins the bell tower to a square watch tower in the north-east corner; from the watch tower a long straight wall walk runs south down the east edge to a stair tower in the courtyard's north-east corner. South-east of the courtyard a barracks and a small armory. Green valley slopes around the crag.
request.style_note: Vesperhold, a half-ruined Gothic castle standing on a rock crag in the middle of a wide mountain bowl, drawn in the same hand throughout: dark-fantasy concept painting, muted slate-grey, ash and moss-green palette with small warm accents of candle and fire light, soft rain haze, confident painterly brushwork with crisp readable architectural silhouettes, massing built from large squared stone blocks with flat faces and clean right angles so every form could be built block by block. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, text or border.
